title: What should the next Lab session build after v0.34.0?
context: v0.32.0–v0.34.0 (flow in the sweep, Atlas modes, Atlas entry points) merged to main on 2026-10-15. NEXT_STEPS.md names the F13LD.sweep flow port next, then HX-1 inertial pressure drop; scope §17 lists them the other way round. Two older items are still open in the code: buckling and crush voxel prep on the main thread (the 2026-10-08 goal), and a handful of small follow-ups. Nothing has moved in Lab or Sweep since 2026-10-15.

options.name: F13LD.sweep flow port
options.summary: Copy 14e, 19g and 19h into Sweep's solver/lab/, flow at 32³ in Fast and 64³ otherwise, append flow columns after the existing ones so F13LD.ingest's validator keeps passing. Vault columns in a later pass.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='40' width='92' height='100' rx='8' fill='var(--muted)' opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='60' y='32' font-size='13' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Lab</text><text x='60' y='78' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>14e 19g 19h</text><rect x='214' y='40' width='92' height='100' rx='8' fill='var(--accent)' opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='260' y='32' font-size='13' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Sweep</text><text x='260' y='78' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>flow cols</text><line x1='110' y1='90' x2='208' y2='90' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='208,84 218,90 208,96' fill='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='80' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>byte copy</text><text x='160' y='165' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>then Vault</text></svg>
pros: It is the order Matt set on 2026-10-15 and has been queued since 2026-10-14.
Puts permeability and wall shear into the database that Vault and surrogate work read from, at sweep scale.
14e, 19g and 19h are close to clean copies: 19g needs only WGPU.device (already in Sweep) and 19h's summary code has no UI ties.
Porting the Stokes-only solver now gives Sweep a fixed copy before HX-1 changes 19g.
cons: 17c's flow job does not copy cleanly: it pulls in the whole worker pool and kernels 13–14 that Sweep lacks. Use the existing no-worker path (buildFlowLinks) or copy 17c and its imports.
Work happens in another repo that is not checked out here; Lab itself gains nothing user-visible.
Once HX-1 lands, 19g changes and Sweep's copy must be re-synced.
options.effort: About 1–2 sessions, mostly in the Sweep repo.
assumptions: Sweep's single-thread link build is fast enough at 32³ and 64³ (it runs once per design, before a solve of under a second).
F13LD.ingest's validator accepts columns appended after the existing ones.
risks: The 17c dependency grows into copying 13, 13b, 13c, 13d and 14 too, widening the byte-copy contract between the repos.
Flow at 32³ in Fast may fall below the grid rule (scope §3.8) on thin-pore designs; the coarse flag must travel with the port.

estimates.basis: 14e, 19g, 19h copy with small guards; Lab's 62-sweep.js:537-554 is a ready template for the caller

estimates.what: Flow time per design in Sweep
estimates.value: about 0.1–0.4 s solve at 64³ on an RTX, plus link build
estimates.basis: scope §12–13: 64³ about 0.09 s per direction bench, 0.35–0.41 s per design measured by Matt

options.name: HX-1 inertial pressure drop
options.summary: Per-axis flow at a list of Reynolds numbers with a mean-velocity force controller, Darcy–Forchheimer fit, Fanning friction factor, unsteady flag, heat-exchanger fluid presets and a long-format CSV (scope §11.2).
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='40' y1='150' x2='300' y2='150' stroke='currentColor'/><line x1='40' y1='150' x2='40' y2='20' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='170' y='172' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>speed</text><text x='14' y='90' font-size='12' fill='currentColor' transform='rotate(-90 14 90)'>dp/dx</text><line x1='40' y1='150' x2='290' y2='70' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><path d='M40 150 Q180 120 290 30' fill='none' stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-width='3'/><text x='230' y='92' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>Darcy</text><text x='190' y='50' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>Forchheimer</text></svg>
pros: The kernel is already fully nonlinear (quadratic equilibrium, Guo forcing); only the driver, cache key and outputs are new.
A ready pass/fail check now exists: Tupin and Ohta refit Castro's measurements with Forchheimer (k and β for gyroid, P and D), which would close the F12 P-gap question.
Serves the heat-exchanger database user directly and is the gate for HX-2 convective heat transfer.
The Reynolds-list blocker is softer than it looks: Castro's experiments span Re 29–145, inside the scope's default 1–200.
cons: Largest of the options: controller, warm start, per-Re cache and results, presets, cards, sweep and long CSV.
Breaks the linear-flow assumptions the cards rely on (fields stored per unit force, wall shear rescaled linearly, cache without fluid), so the Stokes path must be kept separate and unchanged.
64³ is marginal: published TRT runs at Re up to about 200 used about 38 cells per sphere diameter; higher points need 128³ and averaging if unsteady.
assumptions: Matt accepts the scope defaults (1, 10, 50, 100, 200) without the user's operating range, editable later.
The Stokes path stays byte-identical, so cards, sweep and the Sweep port are unaffected.
risks: Compressibility error at higher Re (Mach) and τ near ½ make the top Re points noisy at 64³; results need a resolution flag.
Unsteady onset (Re about 110–250 in periodic packs) forces long time-averaged runs at 128³, tens of seconds per point.

estimates.basis: earlier fluids phases took about one session each; no kernel rewrite, but four layers (driver, results, UI and CSV, validation)

estimates.value: about 5 Re × 3 axes = 15 solves; seconds at 64³, 10–60 s per unsteady point at 128³
estimates.basis: 64³ bench 0.09 s per direction from rest; 128³ 2.9 s per 5,000 steps; unsteady averaging about 10⁵ steps (extrapolated)

options.name: Buckling and crush prep off the main thread
options.summary: The 2026-10-08 goal: crush upload async on the 17c pool (0/1 cube), buckling voxelized once and sent to the axis workers, predict probe timed and moved if slow. Bit-identical checks in validate-prep.js.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='30' width='130' height='34' rx='6' fill='var(--warn)' opacity='0.45' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='85' y='52' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>main thread</text><rect x='170' y='30' width='130' height='34' rx='6' fill='var(--good)' opacity='0.45' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='235' y='52' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>17c pool</text><line x1='85' y1='70' x2='85' y2='120' stroke='currentColor'/><line x1='85' y1='120' x2='225' y2='120' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='225,114 235,120 225,126' fill='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='148' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>no page freeze</text></svg>
pros: Smallest self-contained piece, entirely in Lab; the pattern and pieces already exist (labPrepElasticParallel, _TV_PREP_CACHE, 16b's fallback).
Removes the last page freeze; buckling stops voxelizing once per axis worker.
Easy to verify: bit-identical grids, buckling factors unchanged.
cons: Both features are off by default, so few runs hit the freeze today.
Moves no research question forward and does not touch the fluids track Matt has been driving.
assumptions: Prep, not the solve, is the bulk of the freeze (to profile first, as §1 asks).
risks: 16g's upload has five call sites; making it async can reorder state in the crush run loop.

estimates.basis: same pattern v0.24.0 used for elastic, with the checks already written

evidence.claim: Sweep's solver/lab/ has no flow files (14e, 17c, 19g, 19h absent) and no commits since 2026-10-14, so the port has not started.
evidence.source: GitHub API, mshomper/f13ld.sweep contents and commits

evidence.claim: 17c's flow job depends on the whole worker pool and kernels Sweep lacks; 14e, 19g and 19h copy with small guards, and a no-worker path already exists.
Lab's flow kernel is D3Q19 TRT with Guo forcing and a full quadratic equilibrium; it runs in the Stokes limit only because the force is tiny (g = 1e-5·(64/N)²).
Castro's measurements span Re 29–145; a Forchheimer refit gives k and β for D (8.68e-8 m², 5390 /m), gyroid (2.40e-7 m², 3044 /m) and P (1.31e-7 m², 4035 /m), and Darcy underestimated k by 36–85 %.
evidence.source: Tupin & Ohta, comment on Castro et al. 2019 (Materials)

evidence.claim: TRT with CLI walls on a periodic sphere pack: departs from Darcy at Re_p about 20, unsteady at about 180, and used about 38 cells per diameter with Λ = 3/16 up to Re_p about 200.
evidence.source: Fattahi et al., Pore-scale lattice Boltzmann simulation of laminar and turbulent flow through a sphere pack (arXiv 1508.02960)

evidence.claim: TPMS lattices leave the Darcy regime early: Re about 4 for Primitive, about 20 for Diamond.
evidence.source: Rathore et al., Flow Characterization in TPMS based Porous Geometries: Part 1 (arXiv 2205.03591)

evidence.claim: Buckling and crush prep are still synchronous (16g upload, per-worker voxelization in 16h and 16c); labPrepElasticParallel and _TV_PREP_CACHE exist to reuse.

recommendation: Port first, as Matt ordered: it is one to two sessions, it lands flow in the comparison database before HX-1 changes 19g, and its one snag (17c) has a ready workaround. Then HX-1, which now has a real validation target in the Tupin and Ohta refit of Castro.
change_mind: If the heat-exchanger user is waiting, or Matt wants the Castro P-gap closed before more data goes to Vault, B goes first: the kernel is ready and the Tupin and Ohta β values make it testable now.
